notes: Fiscal year ended 30 June 2025 (FY25, matching data.js 'Jun 2025'). Source is the 'FY25 Annual Report and Appendix 4E' lodged on the ASX on 26 August 2025 (ASX announcements host; fortescue.com's investor pages returned 404 to automated requests and the FY25 file was not linked there). Fortescue reports in US dollars; values converted exactly from US$m. OWNERSHIP: 36.74% of issued capital at 20 August 2025 (shareholder information date), from the substantial holders table, which names Tattarang Pty Ltd, Minderoo Foundation Limited, Nicola Margaret Forrest and John Andrew Henry Forrest jointly. The directors' report gives Dr Andrew Forrest's relevant interest (s205G Corporations Act) as the same 1,131,365,000 shares, and the remuneration report shows that balance unchanged through FY25. A relevant interest is a control-based measure (power over voting or disposal) rather than pure beneficial ownership, so this figure can include shares held by Minderoo Foundation (a charity) and Nicola Forrest; the report does not split it, and it is not split here. Tattarang Pty Ltd (5.73%) and Emichrome Pty Ltd (3.02%) also appear in the top-20 register; they are not listed separately to avoid double counting with the group figure. Nominee and custodian accounts (HSBC Custody Nominees 49.20%, J P Morgan Nominees 7.30%, Citicorp Nominees) are not beneficial owners and are excluded. The Valin Investments (Singapore) and Valin Resources Investments (Singapore) register entries are not listed separately because they appear to sit within Hunan Valin's substantial holding (the report does not say so explicitly). relation 'founder': the board section describes him as 'Executive Chairman and Founder of Fortescue'. BUYBACKS: 0. No shares were bought back under the buy-back program in FY25; the US$163m 'Purchase of shares by employee share trust' buys shares for employee awards and is excluded under the schema rule. DIVIDENDS: US$2,851m (final FY24 A$0.89 and interim FY25 A$0.50 per share, fully franked), matching note (f). STOCK COMP: US$184m share-based payment expense.
